caption: Reference shulker loader (track shulker, hand-built). The dispenser sits ABOVE the box cell X (so the drop, which pops at a random offset and rises, can never leave X upward); a hopper feeds X from the side. A comparator reads X through a stone, in compare mode with a redstone block on its side, so it outputs 15 only when X is completely full; through a stone, two dusts and a repeater it powers a stone beside a sticky piston, which pushes a stone into X: the box breaks and drops with its contents, and the moving stone pushes the drop into the walled drop cell, over the hopper that sends it to the output chest. The piston is two cells from X so that the powered dispenser never powers it (quasi-connectivity). An observer watching the pushed stone's cell fires, through a stone, a dust on the dispenser, which places the next box from its hopper. A start lever, watched by a second observer and delayed 8 gt by a repeater (the first box needs 9 gt to reach the dispenser), places the first box.

Reference shulker unloader (track shulker, hand-built). The dispenser above the box cell X places a full box; the hopper under X empties it into the items chest. A comparator reads X through a stone; a repeater squares it (15 while the box holds anything) onto a dust that feeds a subtract comparator twice: directly on its side, and 4 gt late on its rear. When the box runs empty, the side drops first, so the subtract comparator gives a 4 gt pulse (never on a new full box: then the side rises first). The pulse fires a sticky piston that pushes a stone into X: the empty box breaks and drops, and the moving stone pushes the drop into the walled drop cell, over the hopper that sends it to the empties chest. The same pulse, 2 gt later through a repeater, locks the unloading hopper so it cannot pick the drop up. An observer watching the pushed stone's cell fires, through a stone, a dust on the dispenser for the next box. A start lever, watched by a second observer and delayed 8 gt by a repeater, places the first box.

Flushing shulker loader (track shulker, hand-built): the always-on loader plus a partial-box flush. A comparator reads the feeding hopper; an observer watching that comparator pulses when the hopper runs empty (it is never empty while items flow: it pushes and pulls in the same gt), and through a stone and a repeater (delay 2: a 2 gt pulse would make the sticky piston spit its stone into the cell) the pulse fires the piston, so the box leaves with whatever it holds when the input stops for good (badge flush). When the last item fills a box, both paths fire the piston together. The observer also pulses once at the start (the hopper's first item): the stone goes through the empty cell and back, which places the first box early. The rest is the always-on loader: the dispenser above the box cell, a comparator in compare mode with a redstone block on its side (15 only when full), a sticky piston two cells away pushing a stone into the box, the drop pushed into a walled cell over the collection hopper, an observer on the pushed stone's cell firing the dispenser after each box, and a comparator reading the dispenser through the drop cell's roof with an observer firing it when boxes arrive.

Always-on shulker unloader (track shulker, hand-built): the reference unloader with its start lever replaced by a comparator that reads the dispenser through the drop cell's roof. An observer above that comparator fires the dispenser whenever it goes from holding no box to holding one: it places the first full box by itself, and again whenever full boxes come back after the supply ran out (badges always-on and box-starved). The rest is the reference unloader: the dispenser above the box cell, the unloading hopper under it, a squared comparator reading feeding a subtract comparator directly and 4 gt late (a pulse when the box runs empty, never on a new full box), a sticky piston two cells away pushing a stone into the box, the moving stone pushing the empty box's drop into a walled cell over the empties hopper, the pulse locking the unloading hopper 2 gt later so it cannot take the drop, and an observer on the pushed stone's cell firing the dispenser after each box.

Always-on shulker loader (track shulker, hand-built). A comparator reads the dispenser through the drop cell's roof; an observer above that comparator fires the dispenser whenever it goes from holding no box to holding one, so it places the first box by itself and again whenever boxes come back after the supply ran out. The dispenser sits above the box cell (the drop, which pops at a random offset and drifts, cannot leave upward); a hopper feeds the box from the side; a comparator reads it through a stone, in compare mode with a redstone block on its side, so it outputs 15 only when full; through a stone, two dusts and a repeater it powers a stone beside a sticky piston two cells away (so the powered dispenser never quasi-powers it), which pushes a stone into the box: the box breaks and the moving stone pushes the drop into the walled drop cell, over the hopper to the output chest. An observer on the pushed stone's cell fires the dispenser for the next box. The floor under the box cell and the drop cell's north wall look removable (`circuit shulker shrink` took them out, and most runs pass), but a drop that drifts past them falls out of the machine now and then: they stay.
